sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the next word of a line ("all of its ___"), and the baker can't reason out the answer from meaning. "riches" also already appeared on card 4's question ("gold, silver, precious stones and riches"), so the answer is given away by an earlier card.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The text says only that news will alarm "him", and "he" goes out in fury. The card says it is the king of the North, which settles whether the "he" of vv. 41-45 is the king of the North or the king of 11:36.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: Verse 45 says only "he" will meet his end. The card names him as the king of the North, which settles an ambiguity in the text.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The right answer ("Edom and Moab and Ammon's leaders") is the only one that adds a descriptor like "leaders". The wrong answers are plain lists of three nations, so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

sonnet.problem: This story card only repeats the "shine like the stars forever and ever" line that card 5 just revealed and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and moves nothing forward.
sonnet.rule: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

sonnet.problem: The question says the man dressed in linen is "the one Daniel saw earlier in this vision (Daniel 10:5)". No verse says outright that the two are the same person: 10:5 says "a man dressed in linen" and 12:6 says "the man dressed in linen".
sonnet.rule: He says two names mean the same person only when a verse says so outright, and he gives that verse.
